text:
kevin-corp: Hey team — customers in our on-prem airgapped environment started seeing 502s to the Redwood API after they flipped on corporate TLS inspection. Worked fine before.

ravi: sorry to hear that. quick q: does the proxy do TLS MITM (re-sign certs)? any errors from `curl -v` or SDK logs?

kevin-corp: yes they re-sign. here's the curl we ran from a host behind the proxy:

kevin-corp: ```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
*   Trying 10.0.2.1...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (10.0.2.1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake starts...
* SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
* Closing connection 0
``` 

anya: that SSL error smells like the proxy's re-signed cert isn't trusted by the app, or OCSP stapling failed. can you paste the `openssl s_client` output to see the presented cert chain?

kevin-corp: pasted — proxy is presenting a corporate CA cert. `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` returns the proxy cert with CN=Corp-Intercept-CA and no stapled OCSP. Also SDK logs show `tls: unexpected certificate authority` and the app fails during token fetch (401-ish) intermittently.

ravi: two common paths: 1) trust the corporate CA in the app/container OS trust store OR 2) configure the proxy to allow raw CONNECT tunneling for Redwood endpoints (no MITM). Which is acceptable for your security team?

infra-oncall: also check DNS resolution — are you hitting a private IP from the proxy (10.*) vs Redwood egress hostnames? traceroute shows the proxy forwarding to 10.0.2.1 which is the inspection appliance. If the proxy rewrites SNI or strips it, server name verification will fail.

kevin-corp: sec — we can share our proxy config. they use squid with `ssl-bump` and a PAC file. here's the relevant squid.conf snippet they shared:

kevin-corp: ```
acl SSL_ports port 443
acl localnet src 10.0.0.0/8
ssl_bump peek all
ssl_bump bump all
always_direct allow all
``` 

anya: that `bump all` will force MITM. for Redwood you need either `ssl_bump splice` for `api.redwood-inference.com` or an explicit `acl` + `ssl_bump` rule to `splice` those hosts. example:

anya: ```
acl redwood dstdomain .redwood-inference.com
ssl_bump splice redwood
ssl_bump bump all
``` 

jess: fyi we can provide a short list of hostnames and our published egress IP ranges to allowlist. kevin, I'll DM you the IP CIDRs and host wildcard list.

kevin-corp: thanks. one more wrinkle: some downstream services expect mutual TLS to our private endpoint. after the proxy rewrites certs the server rejects the client cert chain. any suggestions for that case?

ravi: if mTLS is used you cannot MITM. you must `splice` CONNECT or use an explicit tunnel for those hosts. ask security to exempt `*.redwood-inference.com` and `private-redwood.<company>.svc` (if using private endpoints).

infra-oncall: also check firewall NAT/egress allowlist — some customers have transparent proxy + firewall that only allows proxy IPs out. ensure the proxy appliance itself can reach our endpoints on 443 and that DNS returns public IPs (not internal DNS sinkholes). run:

infra-oncall: ```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com
$ traceroute -T -p 443 api.redwood-inference.com
``` 

kevin-corp: ran those; dig returns our corp proxy IP because our internal DNS override points api.redwood-inference.com at the proxy for inspection. will try removing the override for the Redwood hostnames.

squid-bot: ticket created: SUP-8241 — assigned to infra & support. Reference: X-Req: rd-7b2f

ravi: quick mitigation while security approves: 1) add the proxy CA to the application/container trust store (if allowed) OR 2) route only the processes that call Redwood through a host that has direct egress (bypass corporate squid) — e.g., sidecar that tunnels out.

kevin-corp: will try splice rule + DNS override removal. we'll update after tests. thanks for the clear action items and the example `ssl_bump` rule.

nanja (typo corrected to anya): np — lmk if you need the exact hostname list for our private endpoints (we have a couple of edge variants). I'll send them in DM.

jess: DM sent with `*.redwood-inference.com`, `api.redwood-inference.com`, `private-*.redwood-inference.com` and the egress CIDRs.

kevin-corp: follow-up: splice fixed the 502s; app now reports `token exchange timeout` occasionally. next step we will run a tcpdump to see if the proxy is slowing initial TLS handshake/OCSP. I'll open a new thread if we hit perf issues. thanks all!
